The story makes sophisticated use of metaphor and personification to bring the setting to life and mirror the internal state of the protagonist. For example, the train is described as a beast that "screams hoarsely," "spits out" colorful people, and "swallows" others before dragging its "black chain" into the "cave" of the tunnel. Furthermore, the spring clouds are metaphorically compared to "young and flighty fellows" playing pranks, hugging, fleeing, and putting "white caps" on the mountains. The trees have "joints" that crack, and the restless, "fermenting impatience" of the spring weather directly parallels and foreshadows the young man's own internal restlessness and impatience when he arrives at the hotel.
